$description: The idfkit visual identity, in the Design Tokens Community Group JSON module, restricted as the identity standard's contract states: six groups, colour primitives with both themes, colour roles that alias primitives, a usage on every token. Every identity value is written here and nowhere else (FR-002). The file names no touchpoint, no mechanism and no file path.

color.$description: Primitives are the palette; roles are what a touchpoint reads. A role never holds a literal.

navy-950.$description: The darkest navy: the dark theme's page ground and the tile's field.

navy-900.$description: Navy one step up: the dark theme's surface.

navy-850.$description: Navy two steps up: the dark theme's raised surface, a card.

navy-800.$description: Navy three steps up: the dark theme's border and a card's hover ground.

slate-50.$description: The lightest slate: the light theme's surface.

slate-100.$description: Slate one step down: the light theme's raised surface, a card.

slate-200.$description: Soft off-white: the dark theme's body ink and the light theme's border.

slate-400.$description: Mid slate: the dark theme's muted ink.

slate-500.$description: The second muted grey. It fails 4.5:1 on both grounds and is held to 3:1 through the ink-label role (research R8).

slate-600.$description: Dark slate: the light theme's muted ink.

slate-950.$description: Near-black navy: the light theme's body ink and the mark's ink on light grounds.

white.$description: White: the light theme's page ground and the primary action's text in the light theme.

blue-300.$description: Light blue: the end of the cool gradient and the hero scene's ice tone.

blue-400.$description: Blue one step lighter than the accent: a hover tint on the dark ground.

blue-500.$description: The brand blue: the dark theme's accent and the gradient's start in both themes. 3.68:1 on white, so never the light theme's accent.

blue-600.$description: Blue one step darker: the light theme's accent, 5.17:1 on white (research R8).

blue-700.$description: Blue two steps darker: the light theme's pressed accent.

violet-500.$description: Violet: the gradient's middle stop. 4.23:1 under white text, so a surface for nothing that must be read.

red-500.$description: Red: the gradient's end stop, the hero scene's warm tone, and the dark theme's error ink.

red-600.$description: Red one step darker: the light theme's error ink, 4.83:1 on white.

amber-500.$description: Amber: the dark theme's warning ink.

amber-700.$description: Amber two steps darker: the light theme's warning ink, legible on white.

green-500.$description: Green: the dark theme's success ink.

green-700.$description: Green two steps darker: the light theme's success ink, legible on white.

surface.$description: A section or panel one step off the ground.

surface-raised.$description: A card or code block two steps off the ground.

border.$description: A one-pixel rule between surfaces. Not an ink: it is not held to a text ratio.

ink.$description: Body text and headings, on every ground and surface.

ink-muted.$description: Secondary copy: descriptions, captions, metadata set at body size.

ink-label.$description: Labels at 24 px or larger, eyebrows, and non-text elements such as the lockup's divider. Never body text: it meets 3:1 and not 4.5:1 (research R8).

accent.$description: The one brand accent: the primary action's ground, the current link, and emphasis. Same hue in both themes, one step apart (FR-013).

accent-ink.$description: Text set on the accent: the primary button's label. Dark ink on the dark theme's accent, white on the light theme's.

link.$description: An inline link in running text.

focus.$description: The focus ring, a non-text element held to 3:1 against the grounds it is drawn on.

gradient-start.$description: The brand sweep's first stop. The gradient is a surface for nothing that must be read: hairlines, the hero's bloom, a button's glow (research R8).

gradient-mid.$description: The brand sweep's middle stop, at 40 percent.

error.$description: An error message or state, as text on the ground.

warning.$description: A warning message or state, as text on the ground.

success.$description: A success message or state, as text on the ground.

font.$description: One text face and one code face, self-hosted from the standard's fonts directory, each with the fallback stack every touchpoint declares after it (FR-016, research R9).

text.$description: The text face: body, headings, navigation, buttons.

code.$description: The code face, which is also the label face: code, telemetry, eyebrows, and the property name in the lockup (research R7).

text.$description: The text face with its fallback stack, in the order a stylesheet declares them.

code.$description: The code face with its fallback stack.

medium.$description: Labels, the property name in the lockup, emphasised code.

extrabold.$description: Display headings, and the weight the wordmark was outlined from.

space.$description: An 8 px scale. A touchpoint may use any step; it may not contradict one.

half.$description: Half a step: the gap inside a compact control.

1.$description: One step: the gap between an icon and its label.

2.$description: Two steps: a control's padding, a list's gap.

3.$description: Three steps: a card's padding, the page gutter.

4.$description: Four steps: the gap between related blocks.

6.$description: Six steps: the gap between sections of a page.

8.$description: Eight steps: the padding of a hero or a footer.

12.$description: Twelve steps: a section's vertical padding on a tablet.

18.$description: Eighteen steps: a section's vertical padding on a desktop.

radius.$description: Corner radii. Modest: sharper reads as engineering.

sm.$description: An inline code span, a badge's corner, a focus ring.

md.$description: A button, an input, a tab.

lg.$description: A card, a code block, a dialog.

pill.$description: A pill, a dot, a toggle.

elevation.$description: Elevation is told mostly by surface and border; shadows are reserved for what floats.

overlay.$description: A card on hover, a menu, a dialog.

motion.$description: Two easings and three durations. Every duration is set to zero when the visitor asks for reduced motion (FR-017).

out-expo.$description: Large movements: a panel opening, a reveal.

out-quart.$description: Micro-interactions: a hover lift, a colour change.
